title: The Minimum Effective Training Dose Required to Increase 1RM Strength in Resistance-Trained Men: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Androulakis-Korakakis P, Fisher JP, Steele J
population: Resistance-trained men (powerlifting-type squat, bench press and deadlift studies); 6 studies met the inclusion criteria and 5 entered the meta-analysis. Not runners, no women.
findings: From 2629 records, 6 studies met the inclusion criteria; one reviewer searched PubMed, SportDiscus and Google Scholar under PRISMA (PROSPERO CRD42018108911).
All six studies showed that a single set, performed at least once and at most three times a week, was enough to produce significant 1RM strength gains.
The meta-analysis of 5 studies estimated a gain in overall 1RM of 12.09 kg (95% CI 8.16-16.03), of 17.48 kg (8.51-26.46) for the squat and of 8.25 kg (0.68-15.83) for the bench press.

The authors conclude that a single set of 6-12 repetitions at about 70-85% 1RM, 2-3 times a week, to volitional or momentary failure, for 8-12 weeks produced suboptimal but significant squat and bench press 1RM gains in resistance-trained men; they note that it is less clear for the deadlift, for trained women and for highly trained strength athletes.
limitations: Six studies and one reviewer; resistance-trained men only; the lowest-dose arm of each study, for gains in a 1RM, not for keeping strength during a season of other training; sets were taken to failure, unlike a block that leaves repetitions in reserve. No running outcome. Abstract read; full text not read.
implications: Shows that a very low dose (one set, 1-3 times a week) still raises squat strength in trained men, so the 2 sets of a maintenance or lighter session are not a lower bound. It supports a small maintenance dose in direction only; it says nothing on runners, on women or on keeping strength through a taper.
The engine keeps 2 sets for maintenance (f7.maintenanceSets) as a default.
